cards.title: Five-step square-lattice drive
cards.latex: H_n(k)=-J[cos(k dot b_n) sigma_x-sin(k dot b_n) sigma_y]+delta sigma_z; U(T)=prod_n exp[-i H_n T/5]

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf pp. 3-4, square-model Hamiltonian and Fig. 2 discussion

derived_from: partial Fourier transform of the directed A-B hopping sequence
exact exponential of each piecewise-constant step
cards.numerical_form: exact 2x2 Bloch products and dense finite-strip unitary products

checks.reason: The four directed bonds, fifth no-hopping interval and T/5 durations are transcribed from the manuscript.
Every step Hamiltonian is Hermitian and every generated Floquet operator is unitary within 1e-10.
At JT/5=pi/2 and zero sublattice offset the bulk Floquet operator is identity at independent momenta.

open_questions: The text defines delta_AB as an onsite-energy difference while the displayed Hamiltonian uses delta_AB sigma_z; both conventions are evaluated and the discrepancy remains inconclusive.

cards.title: Strip quasienergy and edge localization
cards.latex: U_k(T)|psi_alpha>=exp(-i epsilon_alpha T)|psi_alpha>; w_edge=sum_{y in boundary}|psi_alpha(y)|^2

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf Figs. 2(c) and 3(a-c), with surrounding edge-state discussion

derived_from: open transverse boundary and periodic longitudinal momentum
cards.numerical_form: diagonalize the independently assembled strip Floquet unitary and compute boundary probability

checks.reason: The quasienergy eigenproblem, open-strip geometry and edge-state interpretation are stated around Figs. 2(c) and 3(a-c).
Eigenvectors are normalized and edge weight lies in [0,1].
The trivial, Chern and anomalous representatives respectively show no spanning branch, a pi-gap branch, and branches in both gaps.

cards.title: Full-evolution Floquet winding
cards.latex: W[U]=(1/(8 pi^2)) int dt d^2k Tr(U^-1 d_t U [U^-1 d_kx U,U^-1 d_ky U])
derived_from: closed return-map evolution using the selected quasienergy branch cut
central finite differences on the periodic t-q1-q2 torus
cards.numerical_form: three-dimensional trace integral evaluated from the full unitary evolution, not from a plotted curve

checks.reason: The return-map construction and normalization follow the manuscript.
The three representative phases converge near integer pairs (0,0), (0,1), and (1,1).
The q1,q2 primitive torus has the opposite orientation to Cartesian kx,ky and this Jacobian sign is included explicitly.

cards.title: Floquet-band Chern number and bulk-edge relation
cards.role: T002-T005 and T009 independent topological check
cards.latex: C_n=(1/(2 pi i)) int_BZ Tr(P_n[d_kx P_n,d_ky P_n]); C_n=W(epsilon_above)-W(epsilon_below)
derived_from: sublattice gauge seam sigma_z on the primitive reciprocal torus
cards.numerical_form: gauge-aware plaquette phases of independently diagonalized Floquet eigenvectors

checks.reason: The manuscript states the Floquet-band Chern number and its difference-of-gap-windings relation in Eqs. (1) and (14).
The upper-band Chern sequence is 0,1,0 for the three representative phases.
Chern differences agree with the independently integrated full-evolution winding changes.

cards.title: Weak-drive two-band model
cards.latex: H_0(k)=a(sin kx sigma_x+sin ky sigma_y)+[M-2b(2-cos kx-cos ky)+J cos kx cos ky] sigma_z

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 10 Eq. (18) and Fig. 6 caption

derived_from: partial Fourier transform along y for the cylinder
cards.numerical_form: 2x2 bulk eigensurfaces and block-tridiagonal open-y cylinder Hamiltonian

checks.reason: Eq. (18) and the Fig. 6 caption print the weak-drive Bloch Hamiltonian and all physical coefficients used here.
The real-space cylinder Hamiltonian is Hermitian and reproduces the Bloch Hamiltonian under a periodic-y test transform.
The static upper band has unit Chern magnitude and the bulk grid resolves the one-photon resonance loop.

open_questions: The paper does not print the finite strip width or momentum sampling used for Fig. 6.

cards.title: Repeated-zone Floquet Hamiltonian
derived_from: Fourier harmonics of Delta_0 cos(omega t) sigma_z
cards.numerical_form: Hermitian block-tridiagonal repeated-zone matrix plus an independent midpoint time-product Chern calculation

checks.reason: Eqs. (19)-(20) explicitly give the harmonic drive and repeated-zone Floquet blocks used by the implementation.
The repeated-zone matrix is Hermitian within 1e-12.
A separate real-time midpoint product yields the driven upper-band Chern number zero and is stable to halving the time grid.

open_questions: The paper does not state the repeated-zone cutoff used for Fig. 6(c); M=1 is the smallest truncation that contains the shown resonant replica coupling.
